records.rationale: The diff shows `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED = process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY;`. While its TypeScript type is indeed `string | undefined`, every use in the diff (`if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)`, `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && ...)`) relies only on truthiness, which is correct behavior. The concern about 'accidental interpolation/serialization' is speculative and amounts to a typing/style preference (wrap in Boolean(...)), not a defect introduced by this diff.

records.issue_text: office365calendar CalendarService.ts:258-260 and salesforce CalendarService.ts:90-92 — parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on failure, so the `tokenResponse.success &&` and `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` checks are dead code
records.rationale: Verifiable from the diff: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` when `!refreshTokenResponse.success`, so the callers' subsequent checks are unreachable — in office365calendar `...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)` and in salesforce `if (!accessTokenParsed.success) return Promise.reject(...)` are dead code. Not a defect (behavior is still correct), but it is a specific, accurate observation about unreachable error handling the maintainer may want to clean up or reconsider.

records.issue_text: office365calendar CalendarService.ts:258-260 — Behavior regression: a schema mismatch previously was logged and the credential preserved, but now the refresh throws with a generic message and the MS error body is no longer logged
records.rationale: The diff confirms the regression: the old code used `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` and logged zodError plus the MS response on failure, then continued with `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` so a partial/failed parse preserved existing credentials. The new code routes through `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, which throws a generic `Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` on failure (visible in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts) with no logging of the MS error body, changing behavior from log-and-continue to hard throw and losing diagnostic detail.

records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14 — The outbound request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication (no shared secret header), so the partner endpoint cannot verify the caller and anyone reaching it can request tokens for arbitrary calcomUserIds
records.rationale: The diff's refreshOAuthTokens.ts POSTs to process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with only URLSearchParams body (calcomUserId, appSlug) and no Authorization/shared-secret header, so the outbound sync request carries no authentication; this is verifiable directly in the new file lines. The inbound webhook (app-credential.ts) does check CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, but the outbound path does not, so the described security gap is real, though it may be an accepted design tradeoff (partner endpoint could use other auth outside this diff), so confidence is moderate.

records.issue_text: webhook/app-credential.ts:59-70 — Concurrent webhook calls have a create/create race with no unique constraint to prevent duplicate credentials
records.rationale: The diff shows the handler does prisma.credential.findFirst (with comment 'Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id') and then create/update non-atomically (lines 59-93 of app-credential.ts). Two concurrent webhook calls can both findFirst (both get null) and both create, yielding duplicate credential rows for the same userId/appId. The race mechanism is fully visible in the new code, though the practical impact of duplicates depends on surrounding credential-resolution behavior not shown in the diff.
